claims.text: Treatment converts better than control across all visitors and within every department.
Across all visitors, control shows a higher conversion rate than treatment, yet when visitors are split by department, treatment outperforms control in both groups.
These two results point in opposite directions and should not be read together without understanding how visitors are distributed across departments.
Overall, control averages 0.60 conversion and treatment averages 0.40 — suggesting control wins at the aggregate level.
Within the Easy department, treatment (0.80) outperforms control (0.70); within the Hard department, control (0.30) outperforms treatment (0.20).

The reversal between the overall and department-level results is a known statistical paradox: the department mix likely differs between treatment and control, making the aggregate comparison misleading.
Use the department-level conversion rates as the primary decision metric rather than the overall aggregate The aggregate result is distorted by department mix and would lead to the wrong conclusion

Audit how visitors were assigned to treatment and control within each department to confirm randomisation was balanced Imbalanced assignment across departments is the most likely cause of the conflicting signals
Investigate session minutes outliers to confirm they do not cluster in one group or department Outlier sessions could distort conversion patterns if unevenly distributed
